panels.title: Broker Connectivity
panels.description: mosquitto_up: 1 while connected and the SYS-tree heartbeat is fresh, 0 the instant either fails. See the MosquittoBrokerDown alert.

panels.title: Broker Version
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_info carries the running broker's version as a label; the sample value is always 1.

panels.title: Uptime (current)
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_uptime_seconds - a Gauge (Phase 3 fix), not a counter. Do not rate() this.

panels.title: Broker Uptime - a drop means a restart
panels.description: Watch for a downward step: mosquitto_broker_uptime_seconds only ever decreases when the broker process restarted. See the MosquittoBrokerRestarted alert.

panels.title: Publish Messages Dropped (rate, 5m)
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_publish_messages_dropped_total is a Counter; its healthy value is a constant 0 (DESIGN.md §5.3). Any sustained rate above zero is real signal.

panels.title: Publish Throughput (rate, 5m)
panels.description: received vs sent PUBLISH messages. Fan-out means sent legitimately exceeds received - watch ratio stability, not equality (DESIGN.md §4.2).

panels.title: Exporter Health Counters (increase, 10m)
panels.description: All three read a constant 0 on a healthy broker the exporter fully recognises. Any increase is real, not noise - see the MosquittoUnknownTopicsDetected / MosquittoTrackedTopicCacheFull / MosquittoInvalidPayloadsDetected alerts.

options.content: No latency metric exists for this broker, and none can be derived from its SYS topic tree - it publishes no timing data at all (DESIGN.md §4.2). The panels below are **saturation and backlog proxies**, not latency: growth means delivery is falling behind, not that it is slow.

panels.title: Outbound Packets Queued (saturation proxy, not latency)
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_packet_out_count is a Gauge: packets pending output to the network right now. A sustained upward trend means the broker cannot drain its outbound queue as fast as it fills.

panels.title: Outbound Bytes Queued (saturation proxy, not latency)
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_packet_out_bytes is a Gauge, in bytes pending output right now.

panels.title: Messages Stored
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_messages_stored is a Gauge counting messages currently held (including retained). Sustained growth alongside dropped/queued panels points at accumulating backlog.

panels.title: Connection Load (moving average)
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_load_connections is one Gauge series carrying a window label (1m/5m/15m), not three metrics - the only load/** family kept, because its raw counter is never published anywhere else (DESIGN.md §6.3).

panels.title: Client Counts
panels.description: clients_total and clients_maximum are Gauges (Phase 3 fix - both were miscast as Counters before). Never rate() any of these four series.

options.content: The heap panel below is the broker's own **tracked heap allocations only** - it excludes stacks, allocator fragmentation, shared libraries and TLS buffers, so it reads lower than real process memory and is **not** a substitute for it (DESIGN.md §4.1). This exporter cannot see broker CPU or RSS at all - scrape `node_exporter` / `cAdvisor` / `process-exporter` into this same Prometheus for the real thing, joined on the `instance` label.

panels.title: Broker Heap - tracked allocations only, NOT process memory
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_heap_current_bytes / heap_maximum_bytes. For real broker RSS/CPU use node_exporter / cAdvisor / process-exporter (DESIGN.md §4.1).

panels.title: Exporter Memory (RSS)
panels.description: The exporter's own process_resident_memory_bytes - never confuse this with the broker heap panel to its left.

panels.title: Exporter CPU (fraction of one core)
panels.description: rate(process_cpu_seconds_total[5m]) for the exporter process itself.

panels.title: Bridge Connectivity
panels.description: mosquitto_broker_bridge_connected, labelled by mosquitto_bridge_name. Empty when no bridge is configured. See the MosquittoBridgeDisconnected alert.
